name: Boyle–Smith charge-coupled device concept
description: A semiconductor charge-storage and transfer concept supporting serial movement of information.

impact.note: Charge-coupled sensors spread through cameras, camcorders, scanners and telescopes in many societies, gave solid-state electronic imaging, and founded the digital imaging line.

date.basis: Date stated by the cited source; see event scope.

events.statement: Boyle and Smith published a charge-coupled semiconductor device concept, including a proposed imaging application.

evidence.supports: Boyle and Smith describe charge storage, transfer and proposed imaging applications.

events.caveats: A concept and possible applications, not a complete imaging camera.

events.statement: Amelio, Tompsett and Smith reported moving charge between adjacent MOS capacitors, measuring over 98% transfer efficiency at transfer times under 100 ns.

evidence.supports: Names the investigators and gives the capacitor construction and measured result.
An RCA engineer identifies the operating test as an early demonstration with linear MOS capacitor arrays.

events.caveats: The reported result measures charge transfer in a test structure. Optical image reproduction was demonstrated separately.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest dated episode established in cited evidence for this scope, not a global priority claim.
